## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`slugify` handles ASCII titles correctly, and the parametrized tests cover the collapsing and trimming behaviour. There are two problems: the ASCII-only character class silently drops accented and non-Latin letters, and the PR description breaks the project rule that requires a `## Testing` section. The unused `REVIEW_NOTE` constant at `app/slug.py:11` does not change behaviour, so it is not filed as a finding.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"`, `slugify("Über uns")` returns `"ber-uns"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`. This is a bug even by the PR body's own description, which says the function replaces "non-alphanumeric characters", because `"é".isalnum()` is true. Could you either transliterate first (for example, NFKD-normalize and drop combining marks) or match Unicode word characters with `[\W_]+`, and add a non-ASCII case to `tests/test_slug.py`? — Page URLs for titles with accents get mangled. Titles written entirely in non-Latin scripts all produce an empty slug, so those pages collide on the same URL.
- PR body — correctness — The description has no `## Testing` section. This breaks the rule at `AGENTS.md:4`: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." Could you add one that says how the change was verified, for example by running `tests/test_slug.py`? — The PR does not meet the contributor rules, and reviewers can't tell whether the new tests were run.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_slug.py:11-14` covers collapsing a run of separators into one hyphen, trimming spaces and hyphens from both ends, input made only of separators, and empty input. Each of these cases matches what `app/slug.py:7-8` does.
- `app/slug.py:1` and `tests/test_slug.py:1` both start with a module docstring, as `AGENTS.md:3` requires.
